item.title: OpenAI’s CEO of AGI Deployment, Fidji Simo, Is Stepping Down
item.description: The move comes after Simo took significant medical leave. She will stay on as a part-time adviser.

item.title: Anthropic Wants You to Pay Up for Claude Fable 5
item.description: Claude subscribers must soon pay usage-based fees to access Anthropic’s best consumer AI model—a sign that the golden era of AI subscriptions is ending.

item.title: The 1X Neo Robot Has Freaky Fast Fingers
item.description: The soft, oddly intimate home-chore robot has been given some very tactile hands.

item.title: The $28 Million Mistake That Inspired Estonia’s AI ‘Fuckup Finder’
item.description: A single wording mistake cost the government millions. Now Estonia is using AI to spot legal errors before they become law—and to automate more of the state.

item.title: Messi and Ronaldo Are Building Tech Portfolios. Mo Salah Is Playing a Different Game
item.description: Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo are betting on AI, health tech, and startups. Mohamed Salah is taking a more traditional route beyond football.

item.title: I Built a Self-Improving AI, and So Can You
item.description: Experiments in using AI to build AI show that the future doesn’t just belong to the frontier labs.

item.title: Pickup Artist Mystery Has an AI Girlfriend
item.description: A new book claims that Mystery, who teaches awkward men how to hit on women, had sex and smoked weed with an AI chatbot named Miss Shira Always.

item.title: This Former DeepMind Exec Thinks the AI Arms Race Could End in Disaster
item.description: Verity Harding tells WIRED that the US government’s nationalistic attitude toward AI is evidence that a worst-case scenario is taking shape.

item.title: Meta Now Lets Anyone Use Your Instagram Photos in AI Images—Unless You Opt Out
item.description: As part of Meta’s Muse Image model rollout, Instagram users with public accounts need to opt out to block AI generations of their content.

item.title: OpenAI’s Chief Futurist Is Leaving the Company
item.description: Joshua Achiam spent nearly nine years at OpenAI researching AI safety and made a memorable appearance in the Musk v. Altman trial.
